text:
maria: opened PR 5901 to update Nebula3b model cards: clarify effective long-window semantics, tighten sequence-limit examples, and add an SDK3-friendly embed-shard + rolling-generation pattern. Need a quick cross-team check before I merge.
ryan: can you drop the PR link?
maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5901 
leah: skimmed the diff. i like the effective_window wording. two small asks: 1) make the sequence-limit table show an example for 8k docs (helps product folks), 2) call out memory vs latency tradeoffs for rolling_window=1024 vs 2048.
jin: nit: the Python snippet is currently using `np.mean` without importing numpy — add the import so copy-paste works. also prefer `max_new_tokens` naming in examples (we switched SDK conventions last quarter).
eva: also add a short Compatibility note: quantized variants may route to CPU fallback for embed models on small instances; bench numbers in the card should explicitly say which variant was used (fp16 vs q4). i almost misread the benchmark earlier.
sam: on embed-shard wording, please avoid implying sharding is always better. add a one-liner suggesting the SDK batch helper as the preferred first move, and show shard as a fallback for ultra-long sequences.
maria: plan: switch to max_new_tokens, add numpy import, expand the table with an 8k example, and add the Compatibility callout about quantized fallback + variant tag. i'll add the SDK batch helper one-liner and then keep the shard example as an appendix.
leah: thanks. can we also add a small bench-csv redirect so old links to `nebula3b_bench_v1.csv` don't 404? we had two internal dashboards pointing at it.
maria: yes will add redirects and update the bench link in the doc.
docs-bot: preview site is live for PR 5901 [36mhttps://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr-5901[0m
ryan: LGTM once the import and max_new_tokens rename are in.
jin: left 3 tiny inline comments on phrasing and an example that used `tokens/s` vs `tokens/sec` — normalize them.
maria: copied comments. here's the revised snippet i'll put in (SDK3 canonical):
```python
import numpy as np
from redwood import Client
cli = Client()
# prefer the SDK batch helper for most long texts
embs = cli.batch([long_doc]).embed(model="nebula3b-embed")
# if you must shard manually: create shards and average embeddings
shards = [long_doc[i:i+1000] for i in range(0, len(long_doc), 1000)]
shard_embs = [cli.embed(model="nebula3b-embed", text=s) for s in shards]
merged = np.mean(shard_embs, axis=0)
# rolling-window generation example
resp = cli.generate(model="nebula3b", prompt=long_doc, max_new_tokens=256, rolling_window=1024)
```
maria: i'll add a short Compatibility line: "Quantized variants may route to CPU fallback on small hosts; see runtime-fallback playbook for how to reproduce bench numbers." and hyperlink to the playbook in the PR.
eva: that phrasing reads clear. maybe link to the exact fallback test script too.
maria: good idea, adding link.
docs-bot: CI preview check passed for PR 5901.
maria: merging after CI (if green) and i'll post a roll-forward note tagging eng-ml + eng-runtime so they eyeball the compatibility wording. thanks all for quick reviews!
